title: When the sky splits open.
subtitle: The roof of the world gives way

row.title: the sky will always be there

then: This is one of the earliest Makkan surahs, sent when people openly refused to believe in Resurrection. Ibn Kathir says this refers to the Day of Judgement. {idea}Abu Hurayrah prostrated when he recited it, saying the Prophet ﷺ did the same.{/idea}
now: You plan the mortgage for thirty years, the pension for forty. You treat the world like a fixed stage. {idea}The verse opens with the stage itself breaking.{/idea}
old: The world around me is solid and will carry on as it is.
new: Even the sky will split when Allah commands, so I should not lean on anything but Him.
try: Look up at the sky for a minute today and remember it will one day obey and open.

title: The sky listens to its Lord, as it must.
subtitle: Creation obeys without argument

row.title: listens and obeys
sub: it is right for it to

then: Ibn Kathir says the sky listens to its Lord and obeys His command to split. {reward}It is right for it to obey{/reward}, because His command cannot be rejected or overcome. The surah introduction notes the only right course is to obey.
now: Your alarm goes for Fajr and you hit snooze. The reminder to call your mother sits unread. {idea}The vast sky obeys in an instant. You get to choose.{/idea}
old: I will get round to obeying when I am ready.
new: Everything around me obeys its Lord. Obeying is me fitting in with the universe.
try: Do one thing today the moment you know it is right, without the usual delay.

title: And when the earth is stretched out flat.
subtitle: The ground itself is reshaped
then: Ibn Kathir says the earth will be {idea}expanded, spread out and extended{/idea}. The introduction describes it as plain and smooth on that Day.
now: You close the browser tab, clear the history, keep the second phone in the drawer. {trap}There is always a corner here.{/trap} {idea}On a flat earth there is no corner at all.{/idea}
old: There is always somewhere to keep things out of sight.
new: One day the ground is level and nothing is hidden behind anything.
try: Bring one hidden habit into the light today: drop it, or tell someone you trust.

title: The earth throws out what it held and empties.
subtitle: Every grave gives back its people
then: Mujahid, Sa'id and Qatadah said it throws out the dead inside it and {idea}empties itself of them{/idea}. The introduction adds it throws out evidence of their deeds too.
now: You stand at a funeral and watch the earth close over someone you love. {reward}It feels final.{/reward} {idea}The verse says the ground is only holding them.{/idea}
old: Once someone is buried, that is the end of their story.
new: The earth is keeping them, and it will return every one.
try: Make dua today for one person you have lost, by name.

title: The earth too listens to its Lord, as it must.
subtitle: Sky and earth answer the same call
then: The same words as verse 2 return, now for the earth. Ibn Kathir says the explanation is the same: {reward}it listens and obeys, and it is right for it to do so{/reward}. Next, the surah turns straight to man.
now: The sky above your commute and the ground under your feet are both already obedient. {idea}The only part of the scene still deciding is you.{/idea}
old: Obedience is something only religious people worry about.
new: Sky and earth obey without complaint, and I am the one still choosing.
try: Walk outside today, feel the ground, and choose one act of obedience you have been delaying.

title: O human, you are toiling toward your Lord, and will meet it.
subtitle: All your effort is heading somewhere
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith where Jibril said: {idea}live as you wish, you will die; love whom you wish, you will part; do what you wish, you will meet it.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said whatever you do, you meet Allah with it.
now: The early alarm, the long shift, the night feeds, the commute. {trap}It can feel like running on a treadmill.{/trap} {reward}The verse says it is a road, and it ends with a meeting.{/reward}
old: My daily grind is just survival and leads nowhere.
new: All my effort is a road to my Lord, and I will meet what I did on it.
try: Before work today, make an intention that your effort is for Allah.

title: As for the one handed his book in his right hand.
subtitle: The first of two groups

row.title: you
sub: at the end of the road

row.title: the book in the right hand

then: The introduction says that on that Day all people divide into two groups. {reward}Those whose records are given in their right hands will be forgiven without severe reckoning.{/reward}
now: Results day at school: some students open the envelope and smile. {reward}Imagine the relief of an envelope you are glad to open.{/reward} The work that earns it is happening now.
old: I will just hope it works out when the time comes.
new: The book I receive then is being written by how I live today.
try: Ask Allah tonight to give you your book in your right hand.

title: He will receive an easy reckoning.
subtitle: Shown his deeds, not cross-examined

row.title: interrogation
sub: whoever is questioned closely is ruined

then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith of A'ishah: the Prophet ﷺ said whoever is interrogated in the reckoning is punished. She asked about this verse, and he said {reward}it is the presentation, not the interrogation{/reward}.
now: A kind manager reviews your year, notes the mistakes, and says, "Fine, let it go." {reward}That relief is a small taste.{/reward} Allah's mercy on that Day is far greater.
old: Every single slip I made will be dragged out and judged.
new: Allah can show me my deeds and simply forgive. I ask for that ease.
try: Make this dua today: O Allah, give me an easy reckoning.

title: And he goes back to his family, overjoyed.
subtitle: A homecoming in Paradise
then: Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said he {reward}returns to his family in Paradise{/reward}, happy and delighted with what Allah has given him.
now: Walking through the arrivals gate after a long trip, and your family is waiting. {reward}That rush of joy is the picture here, but it never ends.{/reward}
old: Family reunions are the best thing, and they never last.
new: There is a homecoming where the joy does not end.
try: Call or hug a family member today and say a dua that you meet again in Paradise.

title: But the one handed his book behind his back.
subtitle: The second group

row.title: the man
sub: at the end of the road

then: Ibn Kathir says he will be {trap}given his book in his left hand, behind his back, with his hand bent behind him{/trap}. The surah sets the two groups side by side.
now: You hide the bad report card behind your back as a kid, hoping no one asks. {idea}The verse is a warning given early, so you can still change what is on the page.{/idea}
old: I would rather not think about the bad outcome.
new: Knowing the bad outcome now is what lets me avoid it.
try: Replace one bad deed today with a good one in the same area of your life.

title: He will cry out for destruction.
subtitle: Wishing to vanish instead of face it
then: Ibn Kathir says he calls for {trap}loss and destruction{/trap}. The introduction says they will wish they could somehow die, but they will not die.
now: After a huge mistake you think, "I wish I could just disappear." {idea}Here, that feeling can turn into repentance and a fresh start.{/idea}
old: When I mess up badly, I just want to vanish.
new: Today the answer to shame is turning back, while turning back still works.
try: Turn one regret into a sincere istighfar today.

title: And he will enter the Blaze.
subtitle: The end of the road of denial
then: Ibn Kathir says he enters a blazing Fire and is made to taste its burning. {idea}The next verses explain why: he lived without thinking about the end.{/idea}
now: A warning label on the medicine box is not there to scare you. {reward}It is there so you take the right dose.{/reward} This verse works the same way.
old: Hearing about the Fire just makes me anxious.
new: The warning is there so I take the other road, while I can.
try: Read verse 25 of this surah today and hold on to its hope.
